# Current state — pdf-integrity

What the project believes right now: live terms, constraints, policies and requirements, and what has been found or assessed. Decisions have their own view, `DECISION-HISTORY.md`.

## Terms

### Logical revision

`proposed` · `@audit.term.logical-revision/1` · scope `all`

One user-visible save of the document: the set of xref sections that together represent a single incremental update, ordered oldest to newest. A hybrid-reference save (classic table plus /XRefStm) is one logical revision with two xref sections, and linearization stub structures are not logical revisions. Never equate the raw xref-section count with the number of times a document was edited.

## Requirements

### Evidence renders are deterministic

`proposed` · `@audit.req.deterministic-evidence/1` · scope `all`

All rendered evidence artifacts (revision diffs, annotation on/off diffs, region crops) are produced by the CPU renderer with system-font substitution disabled by default, so that two runs on the same input produce identical pixels. GPU rendering may exist only as an optional fast preview, never as the evidence path.

### Every finding is categorical, explained, and bounded

`proposed` · `@audit.req.explainable-findings/1` · scope `all`

Every emitted finding carries a finding code, an evidence-strength category (structural fact, cryptographic fact, strong derived, contextual indicator, or weak heuristic), a plain-language explanation, and a stated limitation where one exists. The report never emits a single numeric fraud score, and every report states that absence of findings does not prove authenticity.

### The tool never modifies its input

`proposed` · `@audit.req.read-only-analysis/1` · scope `all`

The checker opens inputs read-only and never rewrites, repairs, or cleans a document. All output goes to separate report and evidence files. There is no rollback, deletion, or sanitization feature in any release covered by the current milestones.

### Structural repairs never silently become facts

`proposed` · `@audit.req.repairs-are-visible/1` · scope `all`

Every claim in a report that rests on recovered or repaired structure (rebuilt xref, scanned-for objects, tolerated syntax) is marked as such, and the tool refuses to make cryptographic or revision-history claims when reconstruction is ambiguous. The parse assessment reports strict and tolerant outcomes separately, with the full recovery-event list.

## Observations

### pdf-read surfaces the visual M1 inventory; edit markers remain

`verified` · `@audit.observation.fact-layer-surface-gap/6`

Updated after the visual-fact work: pdf-read now compiles each page's SemanticPage into PageMetrics (text-run counts, visible vs invisible, path/shading paints, image coverage in crop-box basis points, effective DPI of the largest placement) plus document-level FontRecord and ImageRecord inventories. `embedded` on a font means the PDF carries a /FontFile* stream, not that the engine substituted a bundled Standard-14 face. pdf-forensics classifies each compiled page as Vector, RasterOnly, RasterWithTextLayer, Mixed, Blank, or Unknown, and those three former pending sections (page_representation, fonts, images) are gone from the report.

pdf-read now reports: open outcome with recovery events; the %PDF header with its leading-garbage offset; EncryptionInfo; XrefHealth; the trailer /ID pair; every /Info entry with a string value; XMP presence plus the xmpMM media-management lineage; per-page PageStatus including representation metrics; annotation counts per /Subtype; a signature inventory with verbatim /ByteRange and whole-file coverage; seven FeatureFlags; and font and image inventories. Header and /ID are filled on the failed-open path, since neither needs decryption.

Four sections remain pending. Three are structural and cheap: per-xref-section offsets, types and entry counts (needs the XrefSection type from @audit.decision.revision-model, and is really M2 work); linearization; and per-annotation object identity (@lege.work.annotation-forensic-metadata). One is the remaining M1 content-level gap: marked-content edit markers (@audit.work.edit-provenance-facts), which pdf-content currently keeps only for /OC and /ActualText and drops every other tag name, so /TouchUp_TextEdit is not recoverable without a lege-namespace accessor. Signature cryptography is deliberately M4.

The practical consequence: the checker can now say both what lineage a file claims and what a page looks like — vector vs full-page raster vs raster-plus-invisible-text vs blank. For the in-place-editing case that motivated @audit.work.edit-provenance-facts, the DocumentID/InstanceID comparison, the missing-signature-structure finding, and a PDF-Verse-style flattened-export classification are reachable today; the /TouchUp_TextEdit markers and the intra-run font fragmentation are not.

The XMP parser is a targeted scanner in pdf-read's xmp module, not a general XML parser. It matches on local names after the namespace prefix, which is deliberate — the xmpMM prefix is conventional rather than mandated — and accepts a theoretical collision with another namespace defining the same local name in exchange for working on files with non-standard prefixes.

The fixture gap is unchanged: no fixture is encrypted under a non-empty user password on a scheme the standard handler supports, so the password-upgrade half of the encrypted-mode-labelled acceptance check still cannot be tested.

pdf-integrity now lives at lege-pdf/pdf-integrity inside the Lege-ecosystem checkout as its own Cargo workspace, with path dependencies at ../render/crates/*.
